body:
## Finding (P1)

`Patch35_Formation_SetMovementOrder.cs` Postfix has no team filter. `Formation.SetMovementOrder` is called from the async AI tick (`doAsyncAITick -> TickAgentsAndTeamsAsync -> BehaviorXxx.TickOccasionally -> Formation.SetMovementOrder`) for every team's formations. The Postfix calls `TroopStanceManager.ClearStance` which mutates a non-concurrent `Dictionary<int, TroopStance>` (`_stances`). Concurrent `Remove` from a worker thread racing `TryGetValue`/`SetStance` on the main thread can produce `KeyNotFoundException` or silent bucket-chain corruption (.NET Framework 4.7.2 `Dictionary` is not concurrent-safe).

## Fix sketch

Add team filter BEFORE the `_stances.ClearStance(...)` call:
```csharp
if (__instance?.Team != Mission.Current?.PlayerTeam) return;
```
Stances are player-team-only semantically, so the filter is the simpler fix. Alternative: add `lock` to `TroopStanceManager`.

## Finding (P2)

`Main\Features\HeroRace\Hooks\ActionSetCode_GenerateActionSetNameWithSuffix_Patch.cs` has two issues:

1. **Non-static class** â€” declared `public class` instead of `public static class` (line 11). All other TAOM Harmony patches use static classes. Harmony 2 attribute-based patches require static classes; non-static can cause unpredictable application behavior.
2. **Functional no-op** â€” Prefix logic is bit-for-bit equivalent to vanilla `ActionSetCode.GenerateActionSetNameWithSuffix` in `TaleWorlds.Core`. The method is pure string ops with no LOTRLOME-specific behavior; vanilla's `Monster.BaseMonster` resolution already handles custom races. The patch adds per-call overhead on every agent spawn for no behavioral gain.

## Fix sketch

Investigate whether LOTRLOME has a `BaseMonster` quirk vanilla can't handle (use `/research`). If not, **DELETE the patch** per simplicity-criterion ("deletion that holds parity always wins"). If kept for some reason, change `public class` to `public static class`.

## Finding (P2)

`AllianceCampaignBehavior_EndAlliance_Patch` Prefix returns false to prevent alliance dissolution. But vanilla callers (`OnAllianceTimerExpired`, `OnWarDeclared`) proceed to call `AddAllianceDecision` AFTER the (now-skipped) EndAlliance. Result: a "propose new alliance" event for kingdoms that are still allied â€” duplicate alliance proposal in the queue.

## Fix sketch

Either:
- Gate `ShouldPreventAllianceEnd` to alliance-expiry triggers only (not war-declaration triggered EndAlliance calls), so the war-declared path runs vanilla cleanup, OR
- Suppress the downstream `AddAllianceDecision` via a thread-static flag set in this Prefix and read in the caller path.

## Finding (P2)

`DeclareWarAction_ApplyInternal_Patch` Prefix returns false to prevent war declaration. Vanilla `ApplyInternal` dispatches `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnWarDeclared(faction1, faction2, declareWarDetail)` (line 54 in v1.4 decompile) â€” which the patch skips. Listeners (including `AllianceCampaignBehavior.OnWarDeclared` which handles forced alliance ends) receive no notification, leaving downstream state inconsistent.

## Fix sketch

Document the suppression explicitly. If TAOM later "force-declares" a war through its own flow, it must use `DeclareWarAction.ApplyByX(...)` (which goes through the public path and dispatches the event), not `ApplyInternal` directly. Alternative: dispatch `OnWarDeclared` manually from the Prefix when blocking, so listeners see the attempt.

## Finding (P2)

`CavalryChargeService._states` is a `Dictionary` with no lock. In current code Patch31's team filter prevents enemy-team threads from reaching the service, so the race is structurally unreachable today. Mirror `FormationLayoutService`'s pattern:

private readonly object _lock = new();

Wrap `_states` accesses in `HandleChargeOrder`, `Tick`, `GetState`, `OnMissionEnd`. `CavalryFormationState` field mutations (state transitions) also need lock coverage.

## Finding (P2 â€” dormant)

`MBMapScene_GetBattleSceneIndexMap_Patch` uses `static bool _isRetrying` (not `volatile`, not `[ThreadStatic]`) as a re-entry guard. Without `volatile`, the JIT may cache the read in a register and never see writes from another thread. Plus `Thread.Sleep(250ms)` inside a Prefix that fires from a rendering thread = main-thread stall.

Currently inert: category `Patch0_BattleScenes` is commented out in `SubModule.cs:117`. Issue applies if the feature is ever re-enabled.

## Fix sketch

Mark `volatile static bool _isRetrying` or use `[ThreadStatic]` per-thread. Move retry to a background thread. If `Patch0_BattleScenes` stays permanently disabled, add an inline comment noting the safety issue so the next person to re-enable knows.

Drop the param type array and let Harmony find the unique-name overload (only one `AddCharacterToPartyIcon` exists), OR runtime-test that the LogWarning never fires in a normal session.

## Finding (P2)

`CharacterCreationNarrativeStageView_SpawnNonHuman_Patch` (sub-patch inside `CharacterCreationCampaignBehavior_GetYouthMenuArgs_Patch.cs`) has a `[HarmonyFinalizer]` that swallows ALL `NullReferenceException` AND `ArgumentNullException` with `ParamName == "key"`. The intent (per code comments) was "belt-and-suspenders" against horse-data NREs. But the bare `NullReferenceException` swallow masks ANY NRE in the target method â€” including real bugs from unrelated code paths. If the primary defense `RemoveHorseCharacters` works, this Finalizer is dead code. If the primary defense fails, the Finalizer hides which NRE actually fired.

## Fix sketch

Either:
- Tighten scope: set a thread-static flag in `RemoveHorseCharacters` indicating it ran; only swallow exceptions when the flag is NOT set (i.e., primary defense was bypassed), OR
- Remove the Finalizer entirely if `RemoveHorseCharacters` is sufficient (preferred per simplicity-criterion if a session of testing confirms primary defense holds).
